title: CombatMap
description: The root of `combat-map.json`: the ground of the running battle on the game's movement hex grid, written once when the battle begins; the file exists only while a battle is running. Laid out in rows of characters and numbers instead of an object per hex, so the file stays small enough for an AI chat to read whole.

modVersion.description: The four-part version of the mod that wrote the file; the other files match the catalog written by the same version.

exportedAt.description: When the file was last written, in ISO 8601 with the local time's UTC offset.

trigger.description: What caused the export that last wrote the file.

mapId.description: The map's id in the game's metadata database, which keys catalog.json mapDefinitions; a map no star system's contracts are generated on, e.g. a story map, has no entry there. `null` when the map isn't in the metadata database.

hexGrid.description: How the hexes' axial coordinates map to positions in meters, and their neighbors.

terrains.description: The legend of HexRow.terrains: each character's terrain, keyed as in catalog.json terrainDefinitions; `.` is open ground (`null`). A cell's terrain is the first of: map boundary, impassable, destroyed building, deep water, water, the terrain of the building on it, road, the map's custom terrain, forest, rough ground; otherwise open ground.

pathingGroups.description: The groups of the game's pathing capabilities units move with (catalog.json chassisDefinitions.*.movement.pathingId) that block the same steps, by id; HexRow.blockedSteps has an entry per group. The game's own data makes two groups, the mechs' and the vehicles'.

buildings.description: Every building on the map when the file was written, in the order of their ids. A dropship counts only if it had landed by then: hovering or not yet arrived, it occupies no hex, and one landing later, e.g. the Leopard an evacuation calls in, isn't here but can be in the combat state's building lists.

rows.description: The hexes a unit can stand on, by `r`, then `q`; a row of hexes with a gap in the playable area is split in two, and the hexes outside it aren't listed.

ExportTrigger.description: What caused an export. `careerLoaded`: A career is loaded, new or from a save. The game state is skipped while a finished contract's results are still to be applied, and the catalog is rebuilt only when it's missing or stale, once the game has loaded every vehicle, turret and design mask. `manualSave`: The player saves the career outside combat. `autosave`: The game saves the career on its own outside combat, e.g. once an event's popup is closed with the picked option's results applied, or once a contract's results are applied. `contractCompleted`: A contract's results are applied, salvage included, where the game doesn't save the career afterwards, which is `autosave` otherwise. `financialReportShown`: The monthly financial report is shown, with the expenses paid. `mechLabOrderCompleted`: A mech lab order completes, at the end of a day or right away when it has nothing left to do; when several work orders complete together, the last one names the export. `pilotHealed`: A pilot's healing in the med bay completes, as `mechLabOrderCompleted`. `shipUpgradeCompleted`: An Argo upgrade's installation completes, as `mechLabOrderCompleted`. `contractsGenerated`: The game has generated a star system's contracts. `jumped`: The ship has jumped into its destination star system, at the end of that day, with the star system's contracts; work orders completing that day export with it. `arrived`: The ship arrives at the planet after a trip. `storeClosed`: A store closes, from the main screen or the mech lab. `purchaseCompleted`: The store screen completes a purchase, or refuses one. `saleCompleted`: The store screen completes a sale, or refuses one, once for a stack sold at once. `mechBayChanged`: The mech bay changes: a refit, repair, readying or storing is queued, an order is cancelled, the work queue is reordered, a mech or chassis is stored or scrapped, a stored component's repair is queued, or a mech is renamed without a refit. `experienceSpent`: The barracks confirm a pilot's training. `mechPlacementShown`: The game asks where to put a new mech because every mech bay is full, e.g. after salvage completes one. `missionCompleted`: A mission ends, still in combat, before the salvage is chosen. `salvageChosen`: The after-action report has finalized the salvage: once the priority salvage is confirmed, or right away when there is nothing to choose. `shipUpgradeStarted`: An Argo upgrade is bought and its installation starts. `phaseStarted`: A phase begins, before its first unit acts: the battle's first once the lance is deployed, and every later one, also one reached by reserving units. `combatStarted`: A new battle begins, when the briefing is dismissed. `combatLoaded`: A battle is loaded from a save, continuing mid-phase. `activationCompleted`: A unit's activation is done, its attacks resolved; out of contact, once the player's units have all moved. Reserving a unit doesn't count.

HexGridLayout.description: How the hexes lie on the map, spelled out so the file explains itself.

size.description: The distance between neighboring hex centers in meters.

orientation.description: The hexes' orientation: `pointyTop`, rows running along x.

centerFormula.description: The world position of a hex's center, as in the units' positions.

directions.description: The six neighbors' offsets, in the order of the bits of HexRow.blockedSteps.

HexOffset.description: The step from a hex to one of its neighbors, in axial coordinates.

CombatBuilding.description: A building, which units can fire at, stand on and be blocked by.

id.description: The game's building id, as in combat-state.json damagedBuildings.

name.description: The building's name as the game shows it.

position.description: The point the building is placed at, not necessarily its center.

maxStructure.description: The structure of the undamaged building.

MapPosition.description: A point on the map in meters: y is the elevation.

x.description: Along the map's x axis, 0 at the map's center, to 0.1 m.

y.description: The elevation, on the scale of HexRow.elevations.

z.description: Along the map's z axis, 0 at the map's center, to 0.1 m.

HexRow.description: Consecutive hexes of one row, from (q, r) on, one entry per hex in each list.

q.description: The axial `q` of the first hex.

r.description: The axial `r` of every hex in the row.

terrains.description: Each hex's terrain as a character of terrains.

elevations.description: The height in meters a unit standing on each hex is at, a building's roof where one stands, to 0.1 m.

buildings.description: The index in buildings of the building on each hex, or `null`; that entry's CombatBuilding.id is what the combat state refers to the building by.

blockedSteps.description: Per entry of pathingGroups, the steps to neighbors its units can't take on slopes, one character per hex as HexGridLayout.blockedStepsFormula says: too steep a grade between path nodes, too steep ground or a ledge in between. Terrain move costs and units in the way aren't part of it; impassable terrain has its own character in terrains. An approximation: a detour may still reach a neighbor a blocked step can't; a player unit's combat-state.json units.*.movement is exact.
